title: When the Terminal Burns
premise: Astrid Joubert, navigator of the freighter Vela's Mercy, carries a hold full of illegal consciousness backups — refugees from a war Earth officially ended two centuries ago. When the ship intercepts a distress signal in Old Meridian, a language extinct since the war, Astrid and her ragtag crew trace it to a colony that was supposed to be dead. There they discover the war never ended; it was merely muted, and the signal is a peace message from the last living speaker. Pursued by both warring fleets who want the message buried, the crew must choose between loyalty to each other and the truth that could save millions. In the end, Astrid broadcasts the message from inside the dying colony, sacrificing her own backup to shield the transmission, and the surviving crew carry the truth home to a galaxy forced to finally listen.
about_author: Gideon Quintana is a former radio astronomer turned novelist who writes about the silences between stars. He lives aboard a decommissioned research vessel with his partner and an unreasonable number of houseplants.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Astrid navigates the Vela's Mercy through the silent corridors of dead space, establishing the rhythm of her found-family crew: engineer Dov, medic Sefa, and pilot Kesh. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: weary contentment shadowed by the hum of the backups sleeping below decks.

chapters.title: Cargo That Dreams
chapters.summary: During a maintenance cycle, Astrid visits the sealed hold where forty-one consciousness backups sleep in stasis — refugees she smuggled at terrible risk. Kesh catches her there and says nothing. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: guilt braided with tenderness.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: The ship's array picks up a repeating distress call in Old Meridian, a language extinct for two hundred years. Dov's translation matrix half-recognizes it. The crew votes on whether to answer. POV: Dov. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into wonder.

chapters.title: Course Correction
chapters.summary: Against commercial logic, Astrid plots a course toward the signal's origin: Colony Meridian-9, listed as destroyed in the war's final records. The crew argues about what they're risking. POV: Kesh. Emotional beat: fear of breaking their fragile family apart.

chapters.title: What the Charts Refuse
chapters.summary: En route, the crew finds their star charts have been quietly edited — Meridian-9 scrubbed from official records by someone with fleet-level access. Someone wanted the colony forgotten. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: creeping dread.

chapters.title: The Living Ruin
chapters.summary: They arrive at Meridian-9 and find domes half-swallowed by dust — and lights still burning inside. A single figure signals them down: an old woman named Ilsa Vann, last fluent speaker of Old Meridian. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Testimony
chapters.summary: Ilsa reveals the war never ended; a ceasefire was faked so both governments could rearm in secret. She has spent decades composing a verified peace accord in the old language, unforgeable because no one else can read or write it. POV: Ilsa (via recorded testimony). Emotional beat: grief transmuted into iron purpose.

chapters.title: The Message
chapters.summary: Dov decodes the full accord: proof of the false ceasefire plus terms both sides once secretly accepted. Delivering it ends the war; destroying it preserves the profitable stalemate. POV: Dov. Emotional beat: the weight of knowledge.

chapters.title: First Hunters
chapters.summary: A patrol corvette from the Concordat arrives hunting the signal's source. The crew hides the Vela's Mercy in a crater field while Ilsa's ancient jamming buys them hours. POV: Kesh. Emotional beat: terror and the first taste of real stakes.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dov proposes selling the accord's location to buy the crew's safety. The argument splits the family down the middle until Sefa reveals she lost her homeworld to the fake ceasefire. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: betrayal, then reconciliation.

chapters.title: The Hold Opens
chapters.summary: To move Ilsa and the accord, they must wake the backups — revealing to all of them exactly what Astrid has been carrying. The refugees wake confused, grateful, and afraid. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: confession and unexpected forgiveness.

chapters.title: Two Fleets
chapters.summary: Both warring powers converge on Meridian-9, each having traced fragments of the signal. The crew realizes any side delivering the message alone will twist it into propaganda. POV: Kesh. Emotional beat: claustrophobia as the trap closes.

chapters.title: Broadcast Rights
chapters.summary: Ilsa explains the accord must be transmitted simultaneously on open channels from the colony's original array — which requires someone physically holding the relay open while both fleets try to burn the tower. POV: Dov. Emotional beat: resolve hardening around sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Concordat agents board under parley flags and offer Astrid amnesty and new identities if she surrenders the accord. She refuses, but learns they've flagged her cargo — the backups will be seized as evidence either way. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: fury at a system that criminalizes mercy.

chapters.title: Kesh's Choice
chapters.summary: Kesh, who grew up believing the official history, confronts the archives Ilsa kept and breaks — then commits fully to the crew, offering the one skill that matters: flying the relay run through the fleet blockade. POV: Kesh. Emotional beat: faith shattered and rebuilt.

chapters.title: Night Before the Fire
chapters.summary: Quiet chapter: repairs, rationed wine, the refugees teaching the crew Old Meridian songs. Ilsa gives Astrid her own backup drive — 'so someone remembers me correctly.' POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: love made explicit before loss.

chapters.title: The Relay Run
chapters.summary: Kesh threads the Vela's Mercy through the blockading fleets toward the colony's array tower while Concordat and Republic ships exchange first live fire overhead. POV: Kesh. Emotional beat: white-knuckle exhilaration.

chapters.title: Hold the Line
chapters.summary: At the tower, Dov and Sefa fight to keep the relay alive as boarding parties assault the base. Ilsa, dying, speaks the opening lines of the accord herself onto the open channel. POV: Dov. Emotional beat: desperate defiance.

chapters.title: When the Terminal Burns
chapters.summary: Both fleets target the tower. Astrid stays at the terminal, using her own consciousness backup as a shield-buffer to keep the broadcast intact as the array burns around her. The accord goes out whole, in a language two galaxies suddenly remember. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: transcendence through sacrifice.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: The fleets stand down mid-battle as the accord verifies across every channel. Crews on both sides mutiny rather than resume firing. Ilsa dies having heard her language fill the sky. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: stunned, disbelieving relief.

chapters.title: What We Carry
chapters.summary: Weeks later, tribunals begin. The crew, granted clemency for the backups' sake, chooses instead to testify — justice demanded outside the law's bargain. The refugees are recognized as living people, not evidence. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: accountability chosen freely.

chapters.title: The Long Route Home
chapters.summary: The Vela's Mercy flies again, its hold empty and its registry honest. On the last page, Astrid receives a transmission in Old Meridian — thousands of new speakers learning the language Ilsa saved. She answers. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: hope as a practice, not a promise.
